title: Field extension over a separably closed base induces a component bijection
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $L/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $Z$ be any scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Put $Z_L=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A connected component means a maximal nonempty connected subset of the underlying topological space [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The projection $p:Z_L\to Z$ induces a bijection from the set of connected components of $Z_L$ to the set of connected components of $Z$, sending each component to the unique component containing its image. No finiteness hypothesis on $Z$ or $L/k$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the existing separably-closed geometric-connectedness theorem to the morphism `Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))`. Its hypotheses are exactly `[Field k]`, `[IsSepClosed k]`, `[Field L]`, and `[Algebra k L]`, so the spectrum of `L` is geometrically connected over `Spec k`.

Let `p` be the first projection from the displayed pullback. Geometric connectedness is stable under pullback, and the projection is open by the universally-open field-base-change instance. Apply the Mathlib component-homeomorphism theorem `Scheme.Hom.connectedComponentsHomeomorph` to `p`. Its generated `connectedComponentsHomeomorph_apply` equality identifies the resulting homeomorphism with `p.continuous.connectedComponentsMap`; the homeomorphism's bijectivity therefore proves the required bijectivity.
